title: Add resume format detection and validation
description:
Implement the routing layer that detects resume file format from extension (.pdf, .docx, .txt), validates the file exists and is readable, then dispatches to the appropriate parser. Handle unsupported formats with clear error messages.

Acceptance Criteria:
- File extension is detected case-insensitively (.PDF, .Pdf work)
- Supported formats: .pdf, .docx, .txt
- Unsupported formats produce exit code 3 with error listing supported formats
- File not found produces exit code 3 with descriptive error
- File not readable (permissions) produces exit code 3
- Dispatches to correct parser based on extension
- Returns parsed text and metadata (format, word count)
- Function signature: parse_resume(path: Path) -> ResumeContent (Pydantic model with text, format, word_count)

Testing Instructions:
1. Test with .pdf extension - should dispatch to PDF parser
2. Test with .DOCX extension - should dispatch to DOCX parser (case insensitive)
3. Test with .txt extension - should dispatch to text parser
4. Test with .rtf extension - should exit 3 with 'unsupported resume format: .rtf' and list supported formats
5. Test with nonexistent file - should exit 3 with file not found error
6. Verify ResumeContent model has text, format, word_count fields

title: Handle fetch error cases (login walls, CAPTCHAs, network failures)
description:
Implement detection and graceful handling of common fetch failure scenarios: login walls (302 redirects to login pages), CAPTCHAs, JavaScript-heavy pages that don't render, and other access-denied patterns. Provide descriptive error messages with hints.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Login wall detection: pages redirecting to login/signin URLs produce exit code 4 with hint about login requirement
- CAPTCHA detection: pages containing CAPTCHA elements produce exit code 4 with hint
- 403 Forbidden responses produce exit code 4 with hint about bot detection
- Rate limiting (429) responses produce exit code 4 with hint to retry later
- Error messages follow the error/detail/hint format from the error module
- All errors include the original URL for context

Testing Instructions:
1. Test with a URL known to require login - should detect and produce clear error
2. Test with a URL returning 403 - should mention bot detection possibility
3. Test with a URL returning 429 - should mention rate limiting
4. Verify all error messages include the URL
5. Verify error format matches the project error/detail/hint structure

title: Epic: Project Setup & CLI Framework
description: Set up the foundational project structure, CLI argument parsing, API key validation, and error handling framework. Covers FR-006, NFR-005. This epic establishes the skeleton that all other epics build upon.

title: Implement page fetching with timeout handling
description:
Implement the core page fetching logic: navigate to URL, wait for page load, handle timeouts (120s max per NFR-002), handle HTTP errors, DNS failures, and network issues. Return page content or structured error.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Fetches page content from a given URL using Playwright
- Timeout of 30 seconds for page load (contributes to 120s total pipeline budget)
- HTTP 4xx/5xx responses produce exit code 4 with status code in message
- DNS resolution failures produce exit code 4 with descriptive error
- Connection timeouts produce exit code 4 with timeout message
- SSL errors produce exit code 4 with descriptive error
- Returns full page HTML on success
- Function signature: async fetch_page(url: str) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Fetch a known public URL (example.com) - should return HTML content
2. Fetch a nonexistent domain - should exit 4 with DNS error
3. Fetch a URL that returns 404 - should exit 4 with HTTP status
4. Test timeout behavior with a very slow URL or mock
5. Verify error messages include the URL that failed

title: Epic: Resume Parsing
description: Implement resume file parsing supporting PDF, DOCX, and plain text formats. Covers FR-002. Includes format detection, validation, and text extraction from each supported format.

title: Validate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable
description:
Check for the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable at startup before any network calls. If missing or empty, print a formatted error message to stderr and exit with code 5.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY produces exit code 5
- Error message follows the format: 'error: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable not set' with hint
- Empty string ANTHROPIC_API_KEY also triggers the error
- Validation occurs before any network calls or file reads
- Error output goes to stderr, not stdout

Testing Instructions:
1. Unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and run jobfit --url x --resume y - should exit 5 with clear message
2. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='' and run - should exit 5
3. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-test and run - should NOT fail on API key validation (may fail later)
4. Verify error message matches PRD format (error/hint structure)
5. Redirect stdout to /dev/null - error should still be visible on stderr

title: Add verbose progress logging to stderr
description:
Implement step-by-step progress messages written to stderr during the fetch-and-analyze pipeline. Messages should match PRD examples: fetching URL, fetch success with word count, reading resume, parse success with word count and format, sending to Claude, analysis complete. Respect --quiet flag and NO_COLOR env var.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Progress messages are written to stderr (not stdout)
- Messages match PRD format: 'Fetching job posting from URL...', 'Successfully fetched job posting (N words)', etc.
- --quiet flag suppresses all progress messages
- --verbose is default (progress shown by default)
- NO_COLOR env var suppresses any ANSI color/styling in progress output
- Progress function is callable from each pipeline stage
- Word counts are included where specified in PRD
- Function signature: log_progress(message: str) -> None (with module-level quiet/color config)

Testing Instructions:
1. Run full pipeline with defaults - verify progress messages appear on stderr
2. Run with --quiet - verify no progress messages
3. Set NO_COLOR=1 - verify no ANSI codes in output
4. Redirect stderr to file, verify all progress messages captured there
5. Redirect stdout to file, verify progress still visible on terminal (goes to stderr)
6. Verify word counts appear in fetch and parse success messages

title: Set up project structure with uv and pyproject.toml
description:
Initialize the Python project with uv, configure pyproject.toml with all required dependencies (playwright, anthropic, pymupdf, python-docx, click/argparse, rich), set up src/ layout with app package, and configure ruff for linting. Create the entry point module structure.

Acceptance Criteria:
- pyproject.toml exists with correct metadata (name=jobfit, version, python>=3.11)
- All dependencies listed: playwright, anthropic, pymupdf, python-docx, rich
- Dev dependencies: ruff, pytest
- src/jobfit/ package exists with __init__.py and __main__.py
- uv sync completes without errors
- uv run python -m jobfit exits cleanly (even if no-op)
- ruff check . passes with no errors
- Entry point configured: [project.scripts] jobfit = 'jobfit.main:main'

Testing Instructions:
1. Run 'uv sync' - should install all deps without error
2. Run 'uv run python -m jobfit' - should not crash
3. Run 'uv run ruff check .' - should pass
4. Verify pyproject.toml has all listed dependencies
5. Verify src/jobfit/__init__.py and __main__.py exist

title: Set up dotenv for environment variable loading
description:
Set up python-dotenv to load environment variables from .env files.

**What needs to be done:**
1. Add python-dotenv dependency via uv
2. Create .env.sample with documented placeholder values for all required env vars
3. Add .env to .gitignore (if not already there)
4. Add a small utility or entry-point call to load_dotenv() early in app startup
5. Document env vars in .env.sample with comments

**Acceptance criteria:**
- python-dotenv is in project dependencies
- .env.sample exists with all known env vars documented
- .env is gitignored
- load_dotenv() is called at app startup
- Existing code that reads os.environ/os.getenv continues to work

title: Set up Playwright with consumer User-Agent
description:
Configure Playwright browser automation with a realistic consumer-style User-Agent string to avoid bot detection. Set up browser launch with appropriate defaults (headless, reasonable viewport). Install Playwright browsers as part of setup.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Playwright is configured to launch headless Chromium
- User-Agent string mimics a real consumer browser (Chrome on desktop)
- Browser context is created with reasonable viewport (1920x1080)
- Playwright browsers can be installed via setup command or documented step
- Browser launch function is reusable and configurable
- Function signature: async create_browser_context() -> BrowserContext

Testing Instructions:
1. Call create_browser_context() - should return a valid BrowserContext
2. Inspect the User-Agent string - should look like a real Chrome browser UA
3. Verify headless mode is enabled by default
4. Navigate to a test URL (httpbin.org/user-agent) and verify UA string is consumer-style
5. Verify browser closes cleanly after context manager exits

title: Implement plain text resume reading
description:
Implement plain text (.txt) resume reading using Python builtins. Read UTF-8 text files, handle encoding errors gracefully, detect empty files.

Acceptance Criteria:
- .txt files are read and returned as string
- UTF-8 encoding is used by default
- Files with encoding errors are handled gracefully (replace or warn)
- Empty text files produce exit code 3 with clear error
- File not found produces exit code 3 with clear error
- Permission denied produces exit code 3 with clear error
- Function signature: parse_txt(path: Path) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Create a test .txt file with known content - verify reading
2. Test with empty .txt file - should error with exit code 3
3. Test with nonexistent path - should error with exit code 3
4. Test with a file containing unicode characters - should handle correctly
5. Verify returned string matches file content exactly

title: Epic: Job Posting Fetching
description: Implement Playwright-based job posting fetching with consumer-style User-Agent, content extraction, and robust error handling. Covers FR-001, NFR-003.

title: Implement Claude API integration with structured prompt
description:
Implement the core AI analysis module using the Anthropic Python SDK. Design a structured prompt that takes job posting text and resume text, and produces a detailed match analysis covering: overall match score (1-10), skills matrix, experience alignment, keyword analysis, culture fit notes, and tailored suggestions. Use structured output or careful prompt engineering to ensure consistent output format.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Anthropic SDK client is initialized with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
- Prompt includes both job posting text and resume text with clear delimiters
- Prompt instructs Claude to produce all 6 report sections (score, skills matrix, experience, keywords, culture, suggestions)
- API errors (rate limit, server error, invalid key) produce exit code 5 with descriptive messages
- Response is parsed and returned as structured data or raw markdown sections
- Model selection is configurable (default to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 for speed/cost balance)
- Function signature: async analyze_fit(job_text: str, resume_text: str) -> AnalysisResult

Testing Instructions:
1. With valid API key and sample texts, verify API call succeeds and returns analysis
2. With invalid API key, verify exit code 5 with clear error
3. Verify response contains all 6 sections (score, skills, experience, keywords, culture, suggestions)
4. Verify match score is a number 1-10
5. Mock API rate limit response - verify exit code 5 with rate limit hint
6. Verify the prompt clearly separates job posting from resume content

title: Epic: AI Analysis & Report Generation
description: Implement Claude API integration for resume-to-job analysis and structured Markdown report output. Covers FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-007. This is the core value delivery - taking parsed inputs and producing actionable analysis.

title: Implement --output file writing
description:
Implement the --output/-o flag that writes the Markdown report to a file instead of stdout. When specified, write report to the given path. When not specified, write to stdout. Handle file write errors gracefully.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Without --output, report is written to stdout
- With --output path, report is written to that file
- Parent directory must exist (don't create directories)
- Permission denied on output path produces exit code 1 with clear error
- Existing file is overwritten without prompting
- File is written with UTF-8 encoding
- On write success, a progress message indicates where the report was saved

Testing Instructions:
1. Run without --output - verify report appears on stdout
2. Run with --output /tmp/test-report.md - verify file is created with report content
3. Run with --output to a read-only directory - verify exit code 1 with permission error
4. Run with --output to existing file - verify it's overwritten
5. Verify file encoding is UTF-8
6. Verify progress message mentions the output file path

title: Implement DOCX resume parsing
description:
Implement DOCX text extraction using python-docx. Extract all text content from Word documents, preserving paragraph structure. Handle corrupted or invalid DOCX files gracefully.

Acceptance Criteria:
- DOCX files are parsed and full text content extracted
- Paragraphs are preserved with newline separation
- Tables in DOCX are extracted (common in resumes)
- Invalid/corrupted DOCX files produce exit code 3 with clear error
- Empty DOCX files produce appropriate error
- Function signature: parse_docx(path: Path) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Create a test DOCX with known paragraphs - verify extraction
2. Create a DOCX with a table - verify table content is extracted
3. Test with a non-DOCX file renamed to .docx - should error gracefully
4. Test with empty DOCX - should produce meaningful error
5. Verify paragraph separation in output

title: Implement CLI argument parsing
description:
Implement argument parsing using click or argparse for all flags: --url/-u (required, string), --resume/-r (required, string), --output/-o (optional, string), --verbose/-v (bool, default true), --quiet/-q (bool), --help/-h, --version. Validate that required flags are provided and values are sensible.

Acceptance Criteria:
- All flags from the PRD are accepted: --url, --resume, --output, --verbose, --quiet, --help, --version
- Short forms work: -u, -r, -o, -v, -q, -h
- Missing --url or --resume produces exit code 2 with clear error message
- --help prints usage information and exits 0
- --version prints version string and exits 0
- --quiet and --verbose are mutually exclusive
- Invalid flags produce exit code 2

Testing Instructions:
1. Run 'jobfit --help' - should show all flags with descriptions
2. Run 'jobfit --version' - should print version
3. Run 'jobfit' with no args - should exit 2 with error about missing flags
4. Run 'jobfit --url x' without --resume - should exit 2
5. Run 'jobfit --url x --resume y --quiet --verbose' - should error on conflict
6. Verify short flags: 'jobfit -u x -r y' should be accepted

title: Define exit codes and error message formatting
description:
Implement a structured error handling module with exit codes (0-6 per PRD spec) and the error message format: 'error: [brief]\n\n  [detail]\n\nhint: [suggestion]'. Create helper functions for consistent error reporting across the application.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Exit codes 0-6 defined as constants matching PRD spec
- Error formatting function produces: error line, optional detail (indented 2 spaces), hint line
- All error output goes to stderr
- Helper function accepts brief, detail (optional), hint (optional), exit_code
- Module is importable by other components
- NO_COLOR env var suppresses any ANSI color codes in error output

Testing Instructions:
1. Import the error module and call format_error with all fields - verify output format
2. Call format_error with only brief - verify minimal format works
3. Verify exit codes match: 0=success, 1=general, 2=usage, 3=input, 4=network, 5=api, 6=parse
4. Set NO_COLOR=1 and verify no ANSI escape codes in output
5. Verify all output goes to stderr (redirect stdout, errors still visible)

title: Design and implement Markdown report template
description:
Implement the report generator that formats Claude's analysis into the structured Markdown report matching the PRD specification. The report should include: title, overall match score, skills matrix table, experience alignment, keyword analysis, culture fit notes, and suggestions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Report follows exact PRD format with all sections
- Title: '# JobFit Analysis Report'
- Match score section: '## Overall Match Score: N/10'
- Skills matrix is a proper Markdown table with columns: Skill, Required, You Have, Match (with checkmark/cross emojis)
- Experience Alignment section with bullet points
- Keyword Analysis section with bullet points
- Culture Fit Notes section with bullet points
- Suggestions section with actionable bullet points
- Report is valid Markdown that renders correctly
- Function signature: format_report(analysis: AnalysisResult) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Pass a sample AnalysisResult - verify output matches PRD format exactly
2. Verify skills matrix renders as a proper Markdown table
3. Verify match emojis are correct (checkmark for match, cross for miss)
4. Open output in a Markdown previewer - verify it renders cleanly
5. Verify all 6 sections are present in correct order
6. Verify report starts with '# JobFit Analysis Report'

title: Extract meaningful text content from HTML
description:
Extract the main job posting text from fetched HTML. Strip navigation, footers, ads, and boilerplate. Focus on the job description content. Use readability heuristics or HTML parsing to find the main content area.

Acceptance Criteria:
- HTML is parsed and main content area extracted
- Navigation, header, footer, sidebar elements are stripped
- Script and style tags are removed
- Meaningful text is preserved with reasonable formatting (paragraphs, lists)
- Returns clean text suitable for LLM analysis
- Empty/meaningless extraction produces exit code 6 with descriptive error
- Word count is available for progress reporting
- Function signature: extract_job_text(html: str) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Feed a real job posting HTML - verify main content is extracted cleanly
2. Feed minimal HTML with just a paragraph - verify text is extracted
3. Feed HTML with heavy navigation/ads - verify those are stripped
4. Feed empty HTML - should exit 6
5. Feed HTML with only script tags - should exit 6 (no meaningful content)
6. Verify extracted text has reasonable formatting (not one giant line)

title: Implement PDF resume parsing
description:
Implement PDF text extraction using PyMuPDF (pymupdf). Extract all text content from PDF resumes, preserving reasonable structure (paragraphs, sections). Handle common PDF issues like scanned images (detect and warn), encrypted PDFs, and empty documents.

Acceptance Criteria:
- PDF files are parsed and full text content extracted
- Multi-page PDFs are handled (all pages extracted)
- Encrypted/password-protected PDFs produce exit code 3 with clear error
- Empty PDFs (no extractable text) produce exit code 3 with hint about scanned documents
- Function returns extracted text as a string
- Word count is available for progress reporting
- Function signature: parse_pdf(path: Path) -> str

Testing Instructions:
1. Create a simple test PDF with known text - verify extraction matches
2. Test with a multi-page PDF - verify all pages included
3. Test with a non-PDF file renamed to .pdf - should error gracefully
4. Test with an empty PDF - should produce meaningful error
5. Verify word count can be derived from returned text
